$comment: Canonical registry of valid top-level content categories. This file is the single source of truth for: (1) content validation (scripts/validate-content.ts), (2) content/<category> directory names, (3) website navigation. Adding a category here + creating the matching content/<slug> directory is how the taxonomy grows.

categories.name: DevOps Fundamentals
categories.description: Core DevOps concepts and culture questions — the ones that show up early in an interview to check whether a candidate actually understands why the practices exist, not just their names.

categories.name: Linux
categories.description: Linux systems questions covering the command-line fluency and troubleshooting instincts DevOps and SRE roles assume as table stakes.

categories.name: Git
categories.description: Git interview questions on branching strategy, history rewriting, and the recovery commands you actually need when a repository is in a bad state.

categories.name: GitHub
categories.description: Questions on GitHub as a platform — repository administration, permissions, and workflow features beyond plain Git.

categories.name: GitLab
categories.description: Questions on GitLab as a platform — project and permission structure, and how it differs from other Git hosting in day-to-day DevOps work.

categories.name: AWS
categories.description: AWS interview questions built around real production judgment, not service trivia — IAM least-privilege design and incident response, Lambda cold-start and concurrency trade-offs, and S3 exposure prevention and fast alerting. Each thread goes deep on one realistic scenario rather than skimming many services shallowly, covering beginner fundamentals through expert-level architecture and troubleshooting.

categories.name: Azure
categories.description: Azure interview questions on identity, networking, and resource management for teams running production workloads on Microsoft's cloud.

categories.name: Google Cloud Platform
categories.description: GCP interview questions covering IAM (Workload Identity, service account security, org policy versus IAM), Cloud Functions (cold starts, Pub/Sub delivery semantics, Gen 1 versus Gen 2 concurrency), and Cloud Storage (access control, signed URLs, lifecycle management, exposure alerting) — scenario-driven, matching the same depth as this site's AWS coverage rather than treating GCP as an afterthought.

categories.name: Cloud Fundamentals
categories.description: Cross-provider cloud computing concepts — the shared vocabulary and trade-offs that apply before you've committed to any single vendor.

categories.name: Docker
categories.description: Docker interview questions spanning image and build fundamentals (layer caching, multi-stage builds, image size trade-offs), networking (container-to-container connectivity, DNS-based service discovery), and volumes/persistence (bind mounts versus named volumes, data-loss scenarios, backup strategy) — grounded in real debugging scenarios engineers actually hit, not just command syntax.

categories.name: Kubernetes
categories.description: The most extensive topic on this site: RBAC and security context, storage (PV/PVC/StorageClass), workloads and controllers (Deployments, StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, CronJobs), autoscaling (HPA/VPA), scheduling and affinity, networking, cluster architecture, CRDs and operators, admission control, and cluster security hardening. Every question is a realistic production scenario — a pod stuck Pending, a webhook silently breaking scheduling, a StatefulSet rollout behaving unexpectedly — not a bare definition.

categories.name: Helm
categories.description: Helm interview questions covering release management (stuck releases, atomic upgrades, rollback pitfalls), chart authoring (values precedence, subchart overrides, library charts, hooks), and packaging/distribution (versioning, private registries, Kustomize comparison) — the operational edge cases that come up once you're running Helm in a real, multi-team production environment.

categories.name: Terraform
categories.description: Terraform interview questions on provider versioning and the dependency lock file, workspaces versus separate state files, state management (drift, locking, splitting monoliths, sensitive data, backup/recovery), and module design — the kind of state-file and provider-behavior subtleties that only show up after running Terraform against real, shared infrastructure.

categories.name: Ansible
categories.description: Ansible interview questions on idempotency, inventory management, and playbook design decisions that separate a working demo from something safe to run against production hosts repeatedly.

categories.name: CI/CD
categories.description: Tool-agnostic continuous integration and delivery questions — pipeline design, testing strategy, and deployment safety that apply regardless of which CI system you're running.

categories.name: GitHub Actions
categories.description: GitHub Actions interview questions on workflow design, reusable actions, and the permission and secrets-handling decisions that matter once a pipeline touches production.

categories.name: Azure Pipelines
categories.description: Azure Pipelines interview questions on YAML pipeline structure, multi-stage releases, and the approval gates teams rely on for safe deployments.

categories.name: GitLab CI/CD
categories.description: GitLab CI/CD interview questions on pipeline stages, runners, and the caching and artifact decisions that determine whether a pipeline is fast or fragile.

categories.name: Jenkins
categories.description: Jenkins interview questions on pipeline-as-code, plugin and agent management, and the operational realities of running a long-lived CI server in production.

categories.name: Networking
categories.description: Networking fundamentals for DevOps roles — DNS, load balancing, and connectivity troubleshooting across the layers most infrastructure incidents actually live in.

categories.name: Security
categories.description: General security interview questions covering the threat models and hardening practices DevOps engineers are expected to reason about, beyond any single tool.

categories.name: DevSecOps
categories.description: DevSecOps interview questions on shifting security left — pipeline scanning, policy-as-code, and making security a default rather than a gate bolted on at the end.

categories.name: Monitoring
categories.description: Monitoring interview questions on metrics, alerting design, and telling the difference between an alert that's actionable and one that's just noise.

categories.name: Observability
categories.description: Observability interview questions on metrics, logs, and traces as complementary signals — instrumentation decisions, cardinality trade-offs, and building systems you can actually debug in production rather than just watch.

categories.name: SRE
categories.description: Site Reliability Engineering interview questions on SLOs, error budgets, and the incident-response discipline that separates SRE practice from generic ops work.

categories.name: Infrastructure as Code
categories.description: Cross-tool infrastructure-as-code questions on state management, drift, and module design that apply whether you're using Terraform, Pulumi, or something else entirely.

categories.name: GitOps
categories.description: GitOps interview questions on Git-as-source-of-truth workflows, reconciliation loops, and the trade-offs of declarative, pull-based deployment versus traditional push pipelines.

categories.name: Argo CD
categories.description: Argo CD interview questions on GitOps sync behavior, drift detection and reconciliation, and the app-of-apps patterns teams reach for once they're running Argo CD across multiple clusters and environments rather than a single toy deployment.

categories.name: Containers
categories.description: Container fundamentals beyond any single runtime — image layering, isolation mechanisms, and the concepts that underpin Docker, containerd, and Kubernetes alike.

categories.name: Bash
categories.description: Bash scripting interview questions on writing shell scripts that are actually safe to run unattended — error handling, quoting pitfalls, and common footguns.

categories.name: Python
categories.description: Python interview questions focused on the automation and tooling use cases DevOps roles actually need Python for, not general-purpose language trivia.

categories.name: YAML
categories.description: YAML interview questions on the syntax gotchas and structural conventions that matter once YAML is driving Kubernetes manifests, CI pipelines, and IaC config.

categories.name: Databases
categories.description: Database operations questions for DevOps and SRE roles — backup strategy, replication, and the failure modes that come up when you're responsible for a database's uptime, not just its schema.

categories.name: Cloud Architecture
categories.description: Cloud architecture interview questions on designing resilient, cost-aware systems — the higher-level design judgment that sits above any single service or provider.

categories.name: System Design
categories.description: System design interview questions with an infrastructure and operability lens — scaling, reliability, and trade-off reasoning for the kind of design rounds DevOps and platform roles actually run.

categories.name: Platform Engineering
categories.description: Platform engineering interview questions on internal developer platforms, self-service tooling, and the golden-path thinking that defines the discipline.

categories.name: Troubleshooting
categories.description: Cross-cutting troubleshooting scenarios that test systematic debugging under pressure, independent of any single technology stack.

categories.name: Real-World Scenarios
categories.description: Open-ended, real-world scenario questions that combine multiple technologies and force the kind of trade-off reasoning a single-topic question can't capture.

categories.name: Behavioral / DevOps Leadership
categories.description: Behavioral and leadership interview questions for DevOps roles — incident ownership, cross-team collaboration, and the non-technical judgment senior roles are actually evaluated on.
